eclectic

/ih-KLEK-tik/ — rhymes with hectic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something eclectic is made up of a wide variety of different styles, sources, or influences mixed together.

Her eclectic playlist jumps from opera to hip-hop to folk.

Example

A museum curator designed the exhibition to blend Renaissance paintings with contemporary sculptures, vintage photographs, and modern installations—a deliberate eclectic space.

The curator is intentionally selecting and mixing pieces from many different time periods and traditions. 'Diverse' would work, but eclectic more precisely captures the sense that the curator is celebrating and deliberately combining these distinct styles from different sources.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

miscellaneous: Miscellaneous means drawn from many unrelated sources with no organizing idea — the junk drawer of words. Eclectic describes the opposite spirit with the same variety: pieces from many different sources chosen on purpose, so the mix feels curated rather than accidental.

wide-ranging: Wide-ranging says only that the span is broad — wide-ranging interests, a wide-ranging survey. It measures breadth and stops there. Eclectic adds deliberate selection: an eclectic mix is not just broad but chosen from strikingly different styles and sources for the pleasure of combining them.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

uniform: all the same in style throughout

homogeneous: made of parts that are all alike

Where it sits · how wide and deliberate the mix is

uniform → varied → diverse → eclectic

uniform vs. eclectic: Uniform is the opposite end of the scale from eclectic: a uniform collection is all one style, while an eclectic one deliberately draws from many.

varied vs. eclectic: Varied is weaker than eclectic; varied simply means not all the same, while eclectic suggests a wide-ranging mix chosen on purpose from many different sources.

diverse vs. eclectic: Diverse is strong, but eclectic adds something more: a diverse group merely contains many kinds, while an eclectic one is hand-picked from strikingly different styles and sources.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ec- (ek-): out (Greek)

Root — lect: gather, pick, choose (from legein) (Greek)

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of (Greek (-ikos))

Put it together: Greek ek- ('out') plus legein ('to gather, choose') meant 'picking out' — the word originally described philosophers who picked ideas from every school of thought. Something eclectic is characteristically 'picked out' from many different sources and styles.

Use the root in a new word: select: When you select toppings from every section of the salad bar, you literally 'pick them out' — the same choosing root, lect, found in eclectic.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral

Eclectic is the word when you're describing an intentional, thoughtful mix of different styles or sources. Use it for curated collections that celebrate diversity. For a simple mixture without that sense of deliberate curation, 'varied' or 'diverse' often work fine.
